picks.title: A unique shape, a 3D einstein tile, has been discovered
picks.excerpt: AI helped uncover a special object that can fill space without repeating patterns
picks.rationale: AI-assisted discovery of a 3D aperiodic monotile is a fresh, concrete mathematical result; recent math-AI cards covered proofs, curves and sphere packing, never tilings.

picks.title: AI platform and database map protein phase separation across species
picks.excerpt: NTU Singapore researchers used large language models to mine PubMed for phase-behavior data and built PLATO, a database of ~5,118 tested protein sequences, plus PhaseHub, which uses the MolPhase machine-learning predictor to map protein phase separation across 1,106 species (Molecular Plant).
picks.rationale: New open resource (PLATO + PhaseHub) built with LLM literature mining and an ML predictor across 1,106 species; basic biology, no disease target, so it belongs in science.

picks.title: How nature lovers can aid ecology with an assist from AI
picks.excerpt: University of Michigan researchers used ChatGPT and Claude to find and classify species-interaction observations buried in eBird and iNaturalist comments, surfacing signs of nonnative plant spread on the U.S. West Coast; a task taking a student eight hours took Claude six minutes (PNAS).
picks.rationale: PNAS study using LLMs to mine citizen-science notes, with a hard speedup figure (8 hours to 6 minutes); actionable method for any researcher sitting on free-text field data.

picks.title: A new approach to sustainable AI: Offloading part of the computational burden onto light
picks.excerpt: Koç University researchers built two photonic systems that move part of AI computation onto light: a programmable optical neural network that learns from experimental measurements (raising skin-lesion classification accuracy from 68% to 98%) and a multimode fiber laser that processes images at 85-99% accuracy with fewer trainable parameters (Communications Engineering / Communications Physics).
picks.rationale: Two peer-reviewed photonic computing systems (Koç University) with measured accuracy gains; a distinct group and design from the earlier LightTok chip and light-powered deepfake detector.

picks.title: Is 'Attention' the Essence of Intelligence?
picks.excerpt: A mathematical mechanism enables AI models to process language at scale, undergirding the current AI revolution. Our columnist asks: Why is attention the key?
picks.rationale: Quanta explainer linking transformer attention to attention in cognitive science; a credible outlet, a fifth distinct source, and no overlap with the 30-day history (the 10-11 Quanta card was about AI and math).

alternates.title: When Imagining the Future of AI, Gen-Zers Are Not Optimistic
alternates.excerpt: A soon-to-be-published study shows Gen-Zers imagine more worrying than exciting events regarding AI, yet attitudes toward technology and one's politics play a role.
alternates.rationale: A psychology study preview on how Gen Z imagines the future of AI; new data, but it comes from a blog write-up of an unpublished paper.

alternates.title: We're putting too much faith in AI's ability to say no
alternates.excerpt: Today's LLMs are engineered to disobey dangerous requests. But AI refusal is far from foolproof—and could become an instrument of repression.
alternates.rationale: An op-ed on the limits of LLM refusal; credible outlet, but it is commentary.

alternates.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships
alternates.excerpt: Attachment is the term psychologists use for the most significant relationships that hold people's lives together
alternates.rationale: A psychology framing of human-AI relationships; older (10-04) and essay-style.
